B_source.statement:
Let $\struct {P, \preceq}$ be a non-empty [[Definition:Ordered Set|ordered set]] in which every [[Definition:Chain (Order Theory)|chain]] has an [[Definition:Upper Bound of Set|upper bound]].
Then $P$ has a [[Definition:Maximal Element|maximal element]].
This is [[Zorn's Lemma]].

substitutions.the ordered set P: well-ordered subsets of X, ordered by end-extension

derived.a maximal element: a well-ordering of all of X

object_map.reformulation: Apply Zorn's Lemma to partial well-orderings ordered by initial-segment extension.

validity_conditions: The extension order must be by initial segments, so that unions of chains remain well-ordered.
The well-ordering theorem is equivalent to the Axiom of Choice.
proof_plan:
Let $P$ be the set of pairs $\tuple {A, \le_A}$ with $A \subseteq X$ and $\le_A$ a well-ordering of $A$, where $\tuple {A, \le_A} \preceq \tuple {B, \le_B}$ means that $A$ is an initial segment of $B$ and $\le_B$ restricts to $\le_A$.
$P$ contains $\tuple {\O, \O}$.

For a chain, the union of the sets with the union of the orders is a linear order in which each member is an initial segment.
A non-empty subset has a least element found inside any member that it meets, so the union is a well-ordering and an upper bound.
By [[Zorn's Lemma]], there is a maximal $\tuple {W, \le}$.
